reason: The young stars' light seems likely to make the loose nearby gas shine, addressing the first goal.
expectation: I expect the stars to illuminate or ionize the loose cloud, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The dense cloud also faces the stars' light, but the loose cloud seems a clearer place to start.

effect: The loose cloud became an outflow rather than the shining gas I expected; it also shows some nursery material being swept away.
reaction: I was surprised that the result emphasized dispersal rather than illumination.
reason: The dense cloud also faces the young stars' light and may show what remains of the original cloud.
expectation: I expect the dense gas to resist dispersal better than the loose cloud, though it may also glow or be reshaped.

alternatives.reason: Following the outflow into the hot bridge is interesting, but the dense cloud seems more directly tied to the current goals.

effect: The dense cloud became sheltered pillars, completing the goal about what remains of the cloud.
reaction: The contrast between eroded surfaces and protected interiors is satisfying.
reason: The thin cloud fringe is another piece of gas exposed to the young stars and may address the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the stars' radiation to make the fringe glow, though it could instead disperse it.

alternatives.reason: The outflow might further reshape the pillars, but the fringe seems more directly relevant to the remaining goal.

effect: The thin fringe glows as ionized hydrogen captures electrons, showing how the young stars illuminate their surroundings.
reaction: The explanation of the glow was satisfying and matched my expectation.
reason: Dusty gas falling into the smaller system seems directly relevant to the young star's growing disk.
expectation: I expect the incoming dusty gas to add material to the disk, though I don't know what it will become.

alternatives.reason: Following the outflow into the hot bridge is interesting, but I want to see how the smaller system develops.

effect: The incoming dusty gas produced a magnetically guided jet, while the star and disk remain.
reaction: I was surprised that some incoming material was launched outward instead of simply joining the disk.
reason: The new jet may make surrounding gas shine when it encounters the hot bridge, addressing the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the jet to interact with the bridge gas and possibly produce a luminous shock, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The nursery outflow could also interact with the bridge, but I want to follow the newly formed jet.

effect: The jet shocked surrounding gas into glowing, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between glowing gas and another group of stars was a satisfying clarification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making dense cloud pillars was most worthwhile: erosion and shielding explained why some material survives while surrounding gas disperses.

leastWorthwhile.text: Following the jet into the broad bridge was less satisfying because the result said the struck gas could instead have been in the thin fringe, making the specific target feel less consequential.

surprise.text: Dusty gas falling toward the young star produced an outward jet rather than simply adding to its disk.

arbitrary.text: The bridge as the jet's target felt somewhat arbitrary given that the result also allowed the thin fringe; the shock itself had a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting fates of gas and the unexpected jet made me curious about how the smaller system develops.
